chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, and Muhammad ibn Ismail, from al-Fadl ibn Shadhan, from Hammad ibn Isa, from Hariz, from Muhammad ibn Muslim who said:

I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about a woman who sees yellowness during her (menstrual) days. So he said: 'She should not pray until her days have passed; and if she sees the yellowness outside of her (regular menstrual) days, she should perform wudu and pray.'

key_terms.أَيَّامُهَا: her days — refers to a woman's established menstrual cycle (ayyam al-haydh), the regular days on which she is known to menstruate
key_terms.الصُّفْرَة: yellowness (sufra) — a yellowish vaginal discharge that may appear before, during, or after menstruation; its legal status depends on timing relative to the menstrual cycle
key_terms.تَوَضَّأَتْ: she performs wudu — ritual ablution (washing face, hands, wiping head and feet), required before prayer when not in a state of major impurity
key_terms.حَيْض: haydh — menstruation; the state of ritual impurity that prohibits prayer, fasting, and other acts of worship

ai.seo_question: What is the Islamic ruling on a woman who sees yellowish discharge during or outside her menstrual days?
ai.summary: This hadith from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) addresses a jurisprudential question about ritual purity: what a woman should do if she sees a yellowish discharge during and outside her menstrual cycle. The Imam rules that yellowness during her established menstrual days is treated as part of haydh (menstruation) and prohibits prayer; yellowness outside those days requires only wudu and does not prevent prayer. This ruling reflects the broader Shia jurisprudential principle that the rulings of haydh apply only within the woman's customary cycle, while discharges outside that period are treated as non-impure secretions requiring merely ritual ablution.

en.hubeali: Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, and Muhammad in Ismail, from Al Fazl Bin Shazaan, from Hammad Bin Isa, from Hareyz, from Muhammad Bin Muslim who said,

‘I asked Abu Abdullahasws about the woman who sees the yellowness during her (regular menstruating) days. So heasws said: ‘She should not pray Salaat until her (regular) days have passed; and if she were to see the yellowness during other than her (regular) days, she should perform ablution, and she should pray Salaat’.
en.sarwar: 1. Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from his father and Muhammad ibn ’Isma‘il from af-Fadf ibn Shadhan from Hammad ibn ‘Isa from Hariz from Muhammad ibn Muslim who has said the following:

“I once asked abu ’Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, about the case of a woman who finds a discharge of yellow color during the time of her normal period of Hayd (menses). He (the Imam) said, ‘She must not perform Salah (prayer) during the time of her normal blood discharge due to Hayd (menses). If she experiences blood discharge of yellow color in a time, which is other than the time for her normal period of blood discharge due to Hayd (menses), she must take Wudu’ and perform Salah (prayer).’”
